sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 585.7 ± 96.1 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by single-molecule imaging at the cell surface (L1) and by anti-Flag surface staining (L3/L4); no functional (signalling) assay reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: HTR7 has no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–81 extracellular and TM1 begins at residue 82, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus. L1 explicitly states the SNAPf tag was placed 'at its N-terminus' on the full-length receptor and confirmed surface localisation by single-molecule imaging, so insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before M1) is the only position consistent with the stated terminus. No residue number is named in any ledger line, so position_evidence is topology_derived. L2/L3/L4 (Flag surface staining) and L5 (HA-Flag N-terminal) independently corroborate the same junction. Full-length human 5-HT7R with SNAPf fused at the N-terminus (SNAPf-5-HT7R) overexpressed in CHO-K1 cells; single-molecule imaging confirmed receptor at the cell surface. Additionally, Flag-HTR7 (L2/L3/L4) was surface-stained with anti-Flag antibody in RPE1 cells, and HA-Flag-5-HT7R-mScarlet (L5) was constructed with N-terminal HA-Flag tags, all consistent with N-terminal extracellular tagging.

sources.claim: The 5-HT 7 receptor was labeled with the SNAPf-tag ( Keppler et al. , 2003 ) at its N-terminus (SNAPf-5-HT 7 R) and overexpressed in CHO-K1 cells.

literature_notes: Only one extracellular surface site is supported by the ledger. The N-terminal extracellular domain (residues 1–81) is the sole extracellular terminus of HTR7; no signal peptide is present. L1 (SNAPf), L2/L3/L4 (Flag), and L5 (HA-Flag) all converge on the N-terminal prepend position. The C-terminal tags in L5 (mScarlet) and L6/L7/L8 (3xFLAG on rat ortholog) are intracellular and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports a tag in any of the short extracellular loops (ECL1: 141–155, ECL2: 220–238, ECL3: 350–366), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: Rat 5-HT7R C-terminal 3xFLAG tag (pcDNA3.1-3xFLAG) detected by immunocytochemistry in HEK293AD cells; the C-terminus of HTR7 falls in the intracellular region (residues 388–479) and is not a surface site.
mScarlet fused to the C-terminus of human 5-HT7R in pcDNA5-HA-Flag-5-HT7R-mScarlet; C-terminus is intracellular (388–479) and not accessible at the cell surface.
